title: I Accidentally Became the person responsible for an impossible prophecy and Everything Went Wrong
synopsis: A retired assassin tries to run a quiet shop until every customer turns out to be connected to a world-ending prophecy. The story unfolds in The Continent of Borrowed Tomorrows, where time can be borrowed, but the interest is paid in memories. The central problem is a celestial committee preparing an audit of mortal civilization. Pax Dane wants to collect evidence before anyone notices the plot, but every reasonable solution creates a new unreasonable obligation.
premise: A retired assassin tries to run a quiet shop until every customer turns out to be connected to a world-ending prophecy.
authorNotes: I intended to write a dignified fantasy epic. The characters disagreed.

world.name: The Continent of Borrowed Tomorrows
world.rule: Time can be borrowed, but the interest is paid in memories.
world.oddity: Yesterday is legally considered an import.
world.magic: Contract magic turns promises, receipts, and signatures into real spells.
world.threat: a celestial committee preparing an audit of mortal civilization

chapters.title: Nobody Prepared Me For the Extremely Suspicious Cake — Pax Dane POV
chapters.arcTitle: The Problem With The Original Plan
paragraphs: CHAPTER 1 — Pax Dane POV
The Problem With The Original Plan had already produced two meetings, one argument, and a document nobody could legally throw away.
Pax Dane arrived at the forbidden library intending to collect evidence before anyone notices the plot. The plan lasted until the first unexpected detail appeared.
Someone admits that they knew more than they claimed.
Pax Dane had seen stranger things. None of them had been this inconvenient.
The important object was a map. It was not magical in the usual sense, which made it considerably more suspicious.
Pax Dane checked the obvious explanation first. It was wrong. They checked the ridiculous explanation next. It was unfortunately closer.
The world of The Continent of Borrowed Tomorrows followed one inconvenient rule: Time can be borrowed, but the interest is paid in memories.
The conversation became quieter when everyone realized that the newest clue had a date older than the kingdom itself.
There was no screaming yet, which was considered encouraging.
A second person arrived carrying information about the dungeon's legal claim. Their explanation contradicted the first explanation in exactly the way a useful clue should.
Nobody agreed on what to do with the map. One person wanted to destroy it. Another wanted to file it. Pax Dane wanted to know why it had appeared here.
That question led to a small discovery: Pax Dane has a private connection to the border dispute.
The mystery remained open, although Pax Dane now had one useful fact: someone was treating the dungeon's legal claim as if it were a normal administrative matter.
Before leaving, Pax Dane made a decision that would matter later: they would not trust the next official document until they had read the footnotes.
For the first time that day, everyone agreed on something. This was probably going to get worse.
